title: Role Equity and Skills Sponsorship Manual
author: Priya Kapoor
body:
Overview:
This manual describes Redwood's Role Equity and Skills Sponsorship program: a coordinated set of policies, workflows, and tooling that ensures contributors have transparent role expectations, equitable access to growth opportunities, and sponsored learning pathways tied directly to hiring, onboarding, and compensation review cycles. The goal is to reduce bias in promotions, accelerate skill acquisition for high-impact roles, and make role changes predictable for hiring managers and contributors alike.

Audience:
- People Ops
- Hiring managers and IC mentors
- Engineering and Product leaders
- New hires starting in rotational programs

Key Principles (short):
- Clear expectations: every role has a short public role brief, core responsibilities, and 3 measurable success signals.
- Sponsorship over gatekeeping: managers nominate and sponsor contributors into skill tracks rather than relying on opaque approvals.
- Time-boxed sponsorships: skill sponsorships run 8–16 weeks with defined artifacts and a wrap-up review.
- Compensation alignment: successful sponsorship outcomes feed into calibrated compensation pools during the next review window.

Program Components:
1) Role Briefs and Level Rubrics
- Each role (e.g., Backend Engineer II, Product Manager IC3) must have:
  - one-paragraph purpose statement,
  - 3–5 core responsibilities,
  - 4 evaluation indicators (impact, autonomy, scope, mentorship).
- Owners: role steward (typically senior manager) + People Ops. Refresh cadence: annual or after major org reorg.

2) Skills Sponsorship Tracks
- How it works: a manager or senior IC nominates a contributor for a specific skill track (e.g., distributed systems troubleshooting, model-serving performance, customer-facing product design). The sponsor commits up to 10 hours/week of coaching and access to budgeted learning hours.
- Typical track structure:
  - Week 0: Kickoff + baseline assessment (30–60 min)
  - Weeks 1–12: Learning sprints (paired work, reading list, shadowing sessions)
  - Week 6: Midpoint demo and feedback (15–30 min)
  - Week 12: Final artifact + stakeholder review (30–60 min)
- Deliverables: a short technical/behavioral artifact (doc, demo, checklist) and a sponsor letter stating outcome.

3) Decision & Calibration Flow (promotion/role change):
1. Sponsor files Skills Completion Packet in the People Ops queue (Google Forms link in Tools section).
2. Role steward conducts a calibration review with peer stewards (weekly 'Calibration Friday' slot).
3. People Ops assigns compensation band guidance and lists recommended next steps.
4. Final decision communicated in writing to the contributor within 10 business days.

Onboarding and Hiring Tie-ins:
- New hires: during first 30 days, hiring manager assigns an initial role brief and, where appropriate, a 12-week Starter Sponsorship (accelerated onboarding with a skills mentor).
- Rotational hires: rotations default to 8-week sponsorship cycles with a 'rotation outcomes' template.
- Interview feedback: interviewers use the same level rubric indicators; interview debriefs are tagged with recommended sponsorship tracks where gaps are observed.

Operational Details & Tools:
- Primary tools: Greenhouse (hiring), Lattice (performance & development plans), Notion (role briefs repository), Google Drive (artifacts), Slack (#skills-sponsorship), Okta (access), and the People Ops intake form (Google Form).
- Template links (placeholders):
  - Role brief template: https://notion.redwood.company/role-brief-template
  - Sponsorship kickoff template: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/sponsorship-kickoff
  - Skills completion packet: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/skills-complete

Approval & Budgeting:
- Each quarter People Ops allocates a skills sponsorship budget (learning hours + $ per approved track). Typical allocation: $1,500 per approved track + 10 learning hours.
- Approvals: manager + director sign-off for tracks requiring >$3k or cross-team release schedules.

Measure of Success (KPIs):
- Time-to-role-change: median weeks from sponsorship start to role change decision (target: <=14 weeks).
- Conversion rate: % of sponsorships resulting in a role-level move or documented skill upgrade (target: >=45% within 6 months).
- Access equity: % representation of underrepresented groups in sponsorship cohorts (target: increase year-over-year).
- Manager satisfaction: quarterly survey average >=4.0/5.

Example role brief (text table):
- Role: Backend Engineer II
- Purpose: Build and maintain the inference orchestration services that route model requests with latency guarantees.
- Core responsibilities:
  1) Implement and own routing policies for two service domains.
  2) Deliver production-quality observability for request tracing.
  3) Mentor new backend engineers during first 90 days.
- Success indicators: Reduced 95th percentile tail latency by X%, triaged and closed P0 incidents within SLA, led two cross-team design reviews.

Sponsorship Example (short):
- Candidate: Maya Chen (Customer ML team)
- Track: Quantization & Inference Perf
- Sponsor: Marcus Li
- Deliverable: 5-page benchmarking summary, two optimized kernels merged, sponsor letter attached.
- Outcome: Accepted into IC3 role change and eligible for compensation calibration in next cycle.

Templates & Checklists (quick):
- Sponsorship kickoff checklist (examples):
  - Baseline skills survey completed
  - Sponsor and contributor objectives documented
  - Paired sessions schedule
  - Midpoint review calendar invite created

- Final packet checklist:
  - Artifact link in Drive
  - Sponsor letter uploaded
  - Calibration request submitted in People Ops queue

Governance and Escalations:
- If consensus cannot be reached in Calibration Friday, escalations go to the org's Head of People Ops for final binding review within 5 business days.
- People Ops audits every sponsorship for fairness signals: time to decision, representation, and outcomes; quarterly audit report published to leadership.

Communications & Change Management:
- Announce new tracks and budget windows at the start of each quarter via All-Hands and #announcements.
- Managers must archive completed role briefs and sponsorship outcomes to the Notion repository for 3 years to support audits.

Frequently Asked Questions (short):
Q: Who can nominate a contributor?
A: Any manager or senior IC (level 5+) can nominate. Peer nominations are accepted but require manager sponsorship.

Q: How does this affect compensation?
A: Successful sponsorship outcomes are considered during the next compensation calibration. Sponsorship completion does not guarantee a raise but provides documented evidence that factors into calibration pools.

Q: Can contributors self-nominate?
A: Yes, with manager approval and a proposed sponsor.

Appendix: Example Sponsorship Kickoff (template snippet)
- Title: Sponsorship Kickoff: [Name] — [Track]
- Sponsor: [Name] | Manager: [Name] | Start Date: [YYYY-MM-DD]
- Objectives: 1) [skill objective], 2) [artifact to deliver]
- Success criteria (measurable): [x% reduction, y number of merged PRs, z stakeholder sign-offs]

Contact and Ownership:
- Program owner: Priya Kapoor (People Ops) — people-ops@redwood.company
- Operational lead: Marcus Li (Engineering Platforms) — marcus.li@redwood.company

Change log:
- 2024-05-10: Created (initial pilot design).
- 2025-08-04: Added budget table and tightened timelines.
- 2026-02-15: Published program KPI targets and calibration schedule.

Document attachments and artifacts should live in the Notion role-brief repository and the People Ops drive. For questions or to request an ad-hoc calibration, raise a ticket in the People Ops queue or message @people-ops in Slack.
